props.text: The project needs to record its architectural decisions
props.quote: We need to record the architectural decisions made on this project

props.text: Icinga needs to communicate with hosts and services for monitoring to work
props.quote: For our current monitoring to work we need Icinga to be able to communicate with hosts and services

props.text: The team wants to separate code from data to allow open-sourcing code without disclosing implementation details.
props.quote:
We want to separate code from data, so in the future we can open source the code without disclosing our implementation details,
maybe keeping the data in a private Github repository

props.text: The team wants to encrypt sensitive data within the same repository and process.
props.quote:
We want to be able to encrypt sensitive data in the repository: we want to support sensitive data encryption as part of the same
process, without having to manage secrets in a different repository, with different scripts, etc

props.text: The team wants to create Terraform modules to reuse code.
props.quote: We want to create Terraform modules to reuse code

props.text: The team wants to separate Terraform code into different projects to manage infrastructure tiers or application stacks, especially for GOV.UK applications.
props.quote:
We want to separate Terraform code into different projects, each one managing an infrastructure tier or application stack. This
is especially important to separate resources between GOV.UK applications

props.text: The team already runs Puppet on every host
props.quote: This is much easier to manage than having elements of the environment in two places and having two sets of monitoring, Puppet masters, metrics etc

props.text: The migration process doubles as disaster recovery preparation and rehearsal
props.quote: This method much more accurately mirrors a DR situation and so this migration to AWS also doubles as DR preparation and rehearsal as complete environments are built, tested, removed and built again continuously over the course of the task

props.text: Test stacks do not require infrastructure from the existing hosting platform
props.quote: Higher flexibility to test tearing down and bringing up stacks in their entirety without affecting a live service. That is, no test stack will require any infrastructure from the existing hosting platform to support it

props.text: Running on two platforms creates extra work for a long period without a strict migration plan
props.quote: unless there is a very strict migration plan with dates and deadlines, we risk running on two platforms with all the extra work that creates for a long period of time if we don't migrate atomically

props.text: Changes to a Launch Configuration are only propagated to new instances, not existing ones.
props.quote: When the LC of an ASG is changed those changes are only propagated to new instances

props.text: Many instances are long-lived, causing LC changes to take a long time to propagate fully.
props.quote: Historically many of our instances are long lived (e.g. production puppetmaster, at time of writing, has an uptime of 79 days)

props.text: The team uses Terraform to manage infrastructure.
props.quote: There are several possible ways to force propagation of LC changes within the existing Terraform code were considered

props.text: Internal services need internal-only service records to connect without fully qualified domain names.
props.quote:
We have a number of internal services that need to have
internal only service records. This allows clients to connect
within their own environment or stack without needing a fully
qualified domain name

props.text: Internal service records must not be visible outside the local environment or stack.
props.quote: These records should not be visible outside the local environment or stack

props.text: Sister teams use the same approach of buying an unused domain for internal DNS.
props.quote: This is also the approach taken by some of our sister teams

props.text: The MySQL databases receive low traffic, allowing them to be grouped together with capacity safety.
props.quote:
Due to the low amount of traffic most of the 
MySQL databases receive we decided against this due to cost and the number of
instances it would require

props.text: The team has a large, existing investment in using Puppet for managing database tasks.
props.quote:
we do not want to manage individual aspects of databases and their users
using Terraform providers at this date as we have a large, existing, investment in using puppet 
for these tasks

props.text: Centralising databases simplifies connectivity code, connection strings, and secret management.
props.quote:
centralising the
databases themselves in to a single RDS instance in order to simplify our connectivity code,
connection strings and secret management

props.text: Centralising databases is a cheaper approach than maintaining separate instances.
props.quote: This is also a much cheaper approach

props.text: Stagecraft is the only database running on API PostgreSQL instances
props.quote:
The only database that runs on API PostgreSQL instances is Stagecraft, which is
for the Performance Platform

props.text: The main PostgreSQL instance can host Stagecraft because the team does not have the split of vDCs present in the current hosting provider
props.quote:
This is able to run on the main PostgreSQL instance as we do not have the split
of "vDCs" that we have in our current hosting provider

props.text: Work is ongoing to migrate the Performance Platform away from the team's infrastructure to The Government PaaS
props.quote:
Work is ongoing to migrate the Performance Platform away from our infrastructure
and to The Government PaaS, so the long term plan is not have this database in
our infrastructure at all

props.text: AWS environments place Elasticsearch services behind an ELB, making the local proxy layer unnecessary.
props.quote:
In the AWS environments these services are behind an ELB so this layer may
no longer be required

props.text: Testing AWS instances without local proxies shows no service degradation when using ELBs.
props.quote:
We've tested the instances in AWS without the local proxies and we have not discovered any
degradation of service when using the ELBs

props.text: Removing the proxy simplifies networking and application data flow paths.
props.quote:
This means we won't be
testing the exact same thing but will simplify the networking and application 
data flow paths

props.text: Specifying a specific image name ensures the deployed version is known and cannot change without intervention.
props.quote:
This has the benefit that
we know exactly which version we deploy and it cannot change without our intervention

props.text: Security issues from older AMIs are mitigated by overnight security patching deployed via Puppet.
props.quote:
We'd
work around this in the same way we do our other environments; by using the overnight
security patching we deploy via puppet

props.text: ELBs in Amazon handle autoscaling, making dedicated load balancer tiers less useful
props.quote:
In the Amazon world these are less useful as we also have ELBs in place to handle
the autoscaling of instances

props.text: The team wants to reduce networking complexity
props.quote: We want to reduce the networking complexity and remove these machines

props.text: Content Store is the only application that uses the api-mongo cluster.
props.quote: The only application that uses the api-mongo cluster is Content Store

props.text: Removing the api-mongo cluster simplifies the architecture and saves money.
props.quote: Removing the api-mongo cluster will simplify our architecture, and save money

props.text: The router-backend cluster must remain independent due to the critical nature of the Router application.
props.quote:
The router-backend cluster is used by Router. This should remain independent due to the
critical nature of this application

props.text: Rummager is the only application that currently uses api-redis.
props.quote: Rummager uses api-redis

props.text: The historical separation of Rummager into a different vDC is no longer a concern in AWS.
props.quote:
This was traditionally the case because Rummager lived in a different vDC to redis-1/redis-2,
but this is no longer a concern in AWS

props.text: Combining instances saves money by not running multiple Elasticache instances.
props.quote: We will save money on not running multiple Elasticache instances

props.text: The current health check only tests the basic Nginx configuration, causing premature traffic routing to instances where applications are not ready.
props.quote:
The current ALB health check is rudimentary and does only test for the basic Nginx configuration being in place, rather than testing whether
all apps are properly deployed

props.text: Nginx serves 200 OK responses for health checks even when the application port is unavailable, masking deployment issues.
props.quote:
Nginx will serve 5xx responses. The
load balancer still sees the health check responses as `200 OK`, so it continues sending traffic to that instance, even though the application
is not ready to receive traffic

props.text: The health check path is configured in Puppet via the `govuk::app::config` module.
props.quote:
This is configured in Puppet, in `govuk::app::config`, as the `health_check_path`
parameter

props.text: TechOps strategy prioritizes AWS managed services to reduce the burden of managing COTS functionality.
props.quote:
One architectural strategy principle of TechOps is to make use as much as
possible AWS managed services in order to reduce the burden on GOV.UK teams to
manage Commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) functionality/services

props.text: GOV.UK uses MongoDB as the backing database for a number of apps across multiple clusters.
props.quote: GOV.UK uses MongoDB as the backing database for a number of apps

props.text: AWS DocumentDB is compatible with the open source MongoDB API 3.6.
props.quote:
AWS DocumentDB has been developed to be [compatible](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/mongo-apis.html)
   with the open source MongoDB API 3.6

props.text: Non-GOV.UK domains that look like GOV.UK sites or serve content to them may be flagged as phishing by systems like Google's Safe Browsing.
props.quote: In either case, the domain might be flagged as a phishing site by systems such as [Google's Safe Browsing](https://transparencyreport.google.com/safe-browsing/search) technology, which is used by browsers including (but not limited to) Chrome to automatically block requests to the site

props.text: Being flagged as a phishing site could cause a major incident making large parts of GOV.UK inaccessible.
props.quote: At worst, this could cause a major incident, making large parts of GOV.UK inaccessible

props.text: Several Signon domains currently violate the policy by being publicly routable without authentication.
props.quote: A number of Signon domains are currently in violation of this proposal
